notice: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA. All people are fictional. Not real patients and not for clinical use.

babies.medical_history: Born at 30+0 weeks by caesarean section for maternal pre-eclampsia. Received two doses of surfactant for respiratory distress, ventilated for 9 days, then CPAP until day 28. Completed 7 days of antibiotics for culture-negative sepsis in week 2. Fed expressed breast milk with fortifier.
babies.condition_summary: Ex-30-week preterm boy, now 67 days old (corrected 39+4 weeks), with chronic lung disease of prematurity on heated humidified high-flow support and progressive retinopathy of prematurity.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 67. Weight 2280 g. On heated humidified high-flow at 4 L/min, FiO2 0.30, SpO2 91-95%. RR 58/min, mild subcostal recession, no apnoea in 72 h. Tolerating 150 mL/kg/day fortified expressed breast milk by gavage with partial cue-based oral feeds. Chest X-ray: bilateral coarse interstitial markings consistent with evolving chronic lung disease, no new consolidation. Retinal screen on 29 Oct: stage 3 disease in zone II with plus disease in both eyes, progressed from stage 2 one week earlier. Hb 9.8 g/dL. Parents counselled.

oxygen_support.notes: Heated humidified high-flow nasal cannula 4 L/min; weaning trial on 27 Oct failed with desaturation to 84%.

babies.current_care: Special-care cot with continuous pulse oximetry, gavage feeds, multivitamin and iron supplements. Caffeine stopped at 34 weeks corrected.
babies.transfer_reason: Retinal findings now meet treatment criteria and treatment is expected within 72 hours. The referring centre cannot provide this treatment, or the anaesthetic and respiratory support the infant will need around it.

babies.medical_history: Born at 27+3 weeks after spontaneous preterm labour; antenatal steroids complete. One dose of surfactant. Extubated to CPAP on day 6, re-intubated on day 9 for apnoea and rising CO2. Second extubation on day 30 failed within 12 hours.
babies.condition_summary: Extremely preterm girl, 41 days old, ventilator-dependent after two failed extubations, with evolving severe chronic lung disease.
symptoms: rising carbon dioxide on blood gas
babies.clinical_notes: Day 41. Weight 1340 g. Synchronised intermittent mandatory ventilation: PIP 20, PEEP 6, rate 40, FiO2 0.45. Capillary gas pH 7.27, pCO2 68 mmHg. Echo on day 35 limited by poor windows: small restrictive ductus, pulmonary pressure could not be estimated. Furosemide on alternate days. Enteral feeds 120 mL/kg/day with fortifier. Last sepsis screen negative.

oxygen_support.notes: Conventional ventilation via 2.5 mm endotracheal tube; failed extubations on day 9 and day 30.

babies.current_care: Ventilated incubator care, alternate-day diuretic, fortified gavage feeds.
babies.transfer_reason: Two failed extubations and a rising ventilator requirement. The referring unit cannot escalate respiratory support beyond conventional ventilation or assess for pulmonary hypertension on site.

babies.medical_history: Born at 28+1 weeks; ventilated for 14 days, then CPAP. Grade II intraventricular haemorrhage on the left, since resolved. Bilateral inguinal swellings noted from day 50.
babies.condition_summary: Ex-28-week preterm boy, 88 days old, with chronic lung disease on low-flow oxygen and a right inguinal hernia that became irreducible for 40 minutes before manual reduction.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 88. Weight 2410 g. Nasal cannula 0.2 L/min, SpO2 93-96%. Right inguinal swelling became tense and irreducible on 30 Oct and was reduced after 40 minutes under sucrose analgesia; scrotal skin now normal, no bilious vomiting, abdomen soft. Left hernia reducible. Full enteral feeds 160 mL/kg/day. Hb 10.4 g/dL.
babies.current_care: Open cot, oral and gavage feeds, low-flow oxygen.
babies.transfer_reason: Recurrent incarceration risk needs early operative repair. Because of his lung disease and prematurity he is likely to need post-operative ventilation and apnoea monitoring, which the referring centre cannot provide.

babies.medical_history: Born at 25+5 weeks after maternal chorioamnionitis. Ventilated for 21 days, two doses of surfactant. Klebsiella sepsis on day 12 (blood culture positive), completed 14 days of meropenem. Currently on CPAP.
babies.condition_summary: Extremely preterm girl, 51 days old (corrected 33 weeks), on CPAP, with aggressive posterior retinopathy found on her first retinal screen.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 51. Weight 1180 g. Bubble CPAP 6 cmH2O, FiO2 0.32. First retinal screen on 30 Oct: flat neovascularisation in zone I with marked plus disease in both eyes, aggressive posterior pattern. Three to four self-resolving bradycardias per day. Feeds 140 mL/kg/day. Platelets 182 x10^9/L. Cranial ultrasound shows no haemorrhage.

oxygen_support.notes: Bubble CPAP 6 cmH2O via nasal prongs.

babies.current_care: Incubator care on CPAP, gavage feeds, caffeine citrate.
babies.transfer_reason: Aggressive posterior retinal disease needs treatment within 24-48 hours. No treating service is available at the referring centre, and the infant will need intensive respiratory support during and after the procedure.

babies.medical_history: Born at 26+4 weeks; grade III intraventricular haemorrhage on the right on day 3. Ventilated for 10 days. Serial head ultrasounds have shown steadily enlarging ventricles since week 3.
babies.condition_summary: Extremely preterm boy, 59 days old, with progressive post-haemorrhagic ventricular dilatation and rapidly rising head circumference.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 59. Weight 1520 g. Head circumference 31.5 cm, up 2.1 cm in 7 days. Fontanelle full and tense when settled. Cranial ultrasound 30 Oct: ventricular index 4 mm above the 97th centile, anterior horn width 11 mm on both sides. Two lumbar punctures (10 mL/kg each) gave only brief improvement. Apnoeas increased from 1 to 6 per day.
babies.current_care: Incubator care, gavage feeds, daily head circumference and alternate-day cranial ultrasound.
babies.transfer_reason: Ventricular dilatation is progressing despite serial lumbar punctures and needs a temporising cerebrospinal fluid drainage procedure, which is not available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Born at 32+2 weeks by caesarean for placental abruption; received only one dose of antenatal steroid. Grunting from birth.
babies.condition_summary: Moderately preterm girl, 2 days old, with respiratory distress syndrome worsening on CPAP after one dose of surfactant.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 2. Weight 1560 g. Surfactant given by thin catheter at 6 hours. Now CPAP 7 cmH2O with FiO2 rising from 0.30 to 0.55 over 8 hours. Blood gas pH 7.21, pCO2 64 mmHg. Chest X-ray: diffuse ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms. Blood culture sent; on ampicillin and gentamicin. Glucose stable on IV dextrose.

oxygen_support.notes: CPAP 7 cmH2O via nasal mask; FiO2 rising.

babies.current_care: Incubator, IV dextrose 10%, IV antibiotics, nil by mouth.
babies.transfer_reason: Respiratory failure is worsening on CPAP and she will probably need intubation, mechanical ventilation and further surfactant, which is beyond the referring unit's ventilation capacity.

babies.medical_history: Term boy born by assisted vaginal delivery through thick meconium-stained liquor; Apgar 4 and 7. Intubated at 20 minutes for poor respiratory effort.
babies.condition_summary: Term newborn, 1 day old, with meconium aspiration syndrome and suspected persistent pulmonary hypertension.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 1. Weight 3400 g. Conventional ventilation: PIP 26, PEEP 6, rate 50, FiO2 1.0. Pre-ductal SpO2 88%, post-ductal 72%. Oxygenation index 28 on last gas (pH 7.18, pO2 42 mmHg). Chest X-ray: patchy bilateral opacities with hyperinflation. Dopamine 10 mcg/kg/min, mean BP 38 mmHg. Sedated with morphine infusion.

oxygen_support.notes: Conventional ventilation at the maximum settings available locally.

babies.current_care: Ventilated, inotrope, sedation, IV antibiotics, nil by mouth.
babies.transfer_reason: Refractory hypoxaemia with oxygenation index above 25 despite maximal conventional ventilation. Further escalation of respiratory and pulmonary vasodilator therapy is not possible at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Born at 34 weeks by elective caesarean for twin pregnancy (twin 2; twin 1 is well and stays at the referring centre). Mild respiratory distress managed on CPAP.
babies.condition_summary: Late preterm twin girl, 4 days old, who had a tension pneumothorax on CPAP; now has a chest drain with a persistent air leak.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 4. Weight 1940 g. Sudden collapse on 30 Oct with right tension pneumothorax, needle-decompressed and then a chest drain inserted. Drain still bubbling at 24 hours. Now CPAP 5 cmH2O, FiO2 0.40. Repeat X-ray: residual right apical air, lung partly re-expanded. Haemodynamically stable.

oxygen_support.notes: CPAP 5 cmH2O; right intercostal drain on underwater seal.

babies.current_care: Incubator, chest drain care, IV fluids with trophic feeds.
babies.transfer_reason: Air leak persisting beyond 24 hours with an ongoing oxygen requirement. She may need ventilation strategies and a surgical opinion that are not available locally.

babies.medical_history: Antenatal scan at 33 weeks showed a right pleural effusion. Born at 37+1 weeks by caesarean; effusion drained at birth.
babies.condition_summary: Early-term boy, 6 days old, with a congenital right chylothorax that has re-accumulated after two drainages.
symptoms: reduced breath sounds on the right
babies.clinical_notes: Day 6. Weight 2690 g. Right pleural taps on day 1 and day 4: milky fluid, triglycerides 3.1 mmol/L, lymphocytes 90%. Re-accumulated on X-ray today. High-flow 6 L/min, FiO2 0.35. Albumin 22 g/L. Started on medium-chain triglyceride formula.
babies.current_care: Incubator, medium-chain triglyceride formula, albumin infusion as needed.
babies.transfer_reason: Recurrent chylothorax needs a continuous chest drain, prolonged gut rest with intravenous nutrition and possibly octreotide. The referring centre cannot provide prolonged intravenous nutrition.

babies.medical_history: Born at 29+0 weeks after preterm prelabour rupture of membranes 5 days earlier; antenatal steroids complete. Intubated at birth for apnoea.
babies.condition_summary: Very preterm girl, 6 hours old, intubated at birth, with respiratory distress syndrome after one surfactant dose.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 0, 6 hours. Weight 1180 g. Intubated, surfactant 200 mg/kg at 30 minutes. Conventional ventilation: PIP 18, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40. Gas pH 7.25, pCO2 55 mmHg. Temperature now 36.6 C in humidified incubator. Umbilical venous catheter in place, on IV fluids. Mother stable at the referring centre.

oxygen_support.notes: Ventilated via 3.0 mm endotracheal tube; one surfactant dose given.

babies.current_care: Humidified incubator, umbilical venous line, IV fluids, IV antibiotics.
babies.transfer_reason: Very preterm infant who needs ongoing mechanical ventilation and possibly repeat surfactant. The referring centre can only stabilise ventilated infants for a few hours.

babies.medical_history: Term boy; prolonged second stage with fetal bradycardia and cord prolapse. Apgar 2, 4 and 6. Needed intubation and 60 seconds of chest compressions.
babies.condition_summary: Term newborn, 3 hours old, with moderate encephalopathy after perinatal asphyxia; still within the 6-hour window for cooling.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 0, 3 hours. Weight 3250 g. Cord arterial pH 6.92, base deficit 16. Extubated at 40 minutes, now breathing room air. Modified Sarnat: lethargic, reduced tone, weak suck and Moro, constricted pupils, consistent with moderate encephalopathy. No seizures seen yet. Passive cooling started (target rectal 33.5-34.5 C, currently 34.9 C). Glucose 3.8 mmol/L.

oxygen_support.notes: Self-ventilating in room air after brief intubation at birth.

babies.current_care: Passive cooling with rectal temperature monitoring, IV fluids at 40 mL/kg/day, nil by mouth.
babies.transfer_reason: Meets criteria for therapeutic hypothermia, which must start within 6 hours of birth with brain monitoring. The referring centre cannot provide servo-controlled cooling.

babies.medical_history: Born at 38+2 weeks after maternal uterine rupture; Apgar 1, 2 and 4. Prolonged resuscitation including adrenaline.
babies.condition_summary: Term girl, 1 day old, with severe encephalopathy, recurrent seizures and multi-organ dysfunction after perinatal asphyxia.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 1. Weight 2900 g. Ventilated, FiO2 0.30. Passive cooling started at 4 hours; temperature control erratic (33.1-35.2 C). Three clinical seizures treated with phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg and a further 10 mg/kg. Urine output 0.4 mL/kg/h. Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. INR 2.6, platelets 70 x10^9/L. ALT 820 U/L.

oxygen_support.notes: Ventilated for poor respiratory drive and seizures.

babies.current_care: Ventilated, passive cooling, phenobarbitone, fluid restriction, fresh frozen plasma given.
babies.transfer_reason: Severe encephalopathy with ongoing seizures, kidney and clotting involvement and unstable passive cooling. She needs controlled cooling, continuous brain monitoring and multi-organ support that the referring centre does not have.

babies.medical_history: Term boy with moderate encephalopathy after shoulder dystocia; cooled for 72 hours at the referring centre with a manual gel-pack method and rewarmed on day 4.
babies.condition_summary: Term boy, 7 days old, after 72 hours of cooling for moderate encephalopathy, with persistent poor feeding and abnormal tone.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 7. Weight 3420 g. Rewarmed without problems on day 4. One 40-second right-sided clonic seizure on day 5, loaded with levetiracetam, none since. Taking 60% of feeds orally, the rest by tube. Tone: head lag with increased limb tone. Breathing room air. No MRI available locally.
babies.current_care: Open cot, levetiracetam, partial tube feeds.
babies.transfer_reason: Needs a brain MRI, an EEG and a neurology review to guide prognosis and seizure management; none of these are available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Term boy with unremarkable antenatal scans. Went home with his mother on day 1 and returned on day 2 with poor feeding and grey colour.
babies.condition_summary: Term boy, 2 days old, in shock with weak femoral pulses; suspected duct-dependent left heart obstruction, started on prostaglandin.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 2. Weight 3010 g. Arrived in shock: lactate 7.8 mmol/L, pH 7.12. Right arm BP 72/40, leg BP 41/25. Femoral pulses barely palpable. Bedside screening suggests narrowing of the aortic arch; formal echocardiography not available. Alprostadil 0.05 mcg/kg/min started at 14:00. One apnoea after starting it; now on CPAP, FiO2 0.21. Lactate improving to 3.4 mmol/L. Dopamine 5 mcg/kg/min.

oxygen_support.notes: CPAP 5 cmH2O after a prostaglandin-related apnoea.

babies.current_care: Prostaglandin infusion, inotrope, IV fluids, nil by mouth.
babies.transfer_reason: Suspected critical aortic arch obstruction dependent on prostaglandin. Needs confirmatory echocardiography and cardiac surgical planning, which are not available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Term girl; the 20-week scan reported 'parallel great arteries' but the follow-up scan was missed.
babies.condition_summary: Term newborn, 1 day old, with profound cyanosis that does not respond to oxygen; suspected transposition of the great arteries.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 1. Weight 3250 g. SpO2 65-70% in upper and lower limbs, with minimal change on 100% oxygen (hyperoxia test pO2 38 mmHg). Chest X-ray: narrow upper mediastinum. No murmur. Alprostadil 0.05 mcg/kg/min started; SpO2 now 72%. Lactate 3.9 mmol/L and rising.

oxygen_support.notes: Low-flow oxygen 0.5 L/min with minimal response.

babies.current_care: Prostaglandin infusion, IV fluids, close observation in the high-dependency area.
babies.transfer_reason: Profound cyanosis with probable transposition and rising lactate. She is likely to need an atrial septostomy within hours and later surgery, neither of which is available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Born at 37 weeks; trisomy 21 diagnosed after birth (karyotype confirmed). Murmur heard on day 3; local echo reported a large atrioventricular septal defect.
babies.condition_summary: Term boy with trisomy 21, 21 days old, with a complete atrioventricular septal defect and worsening heart failure.
symptoms: liver edge 3 cm below costal margin
babies.clinical_notes: Day 21. Weight 2780 g (birth weight 2700 g). Furosemide 1 mg/kg twice daily and spironolactone. Feeds 120 mL/kg/day but each feed takes 40 minutes. Liver 3 cm below the costal margin. SpO2 94% in room air. Thyroid function normal. Pulmonary pressure has not been assessed.
babies.current_care: Diuretics, nasogastric top-up feeds, calorie-dense formula.
babies.transfer_reason: Faltering growth and progressive heart failure despite diuretics. Needs cardiology assessment, evaluation of pulmonary pressures and decisions about the timing of surgery.

babies.medical_history: Late preterm girl. Fetal echocardiography at 24 weeks diagnosed pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum. Delivery was planned at a cardiac centre but labour progressed rapidly at the referring centre.
babies.condition_summary: Late preterm newborn, 4 hours old, with antenatally diagnosed duct-dependent pulmonary circulation, on prostaglandin.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 0, 4 hours. Weight 2450 g. Alprostadil 0.02 mcg/kg/min started at 1 hour; SpO2 76-80%. No respiratory distress, RR 52/min. Glucose 2.4 mmol/L at 2 hours, corrected with IV dextrose. Umbilical venous line in place. No apnoea so far.

oxygen_support.notes: Room air; saturation target 75-85% while on prostaglandin.

babies.current_care: Prostaglandin infusion via umbilical venous line, IV dextrose 10%.
babies.transfer_reason: Duct-dependent pulmonary blood flow with an antenatally planned cardiac pathway. Needs a cardiac centre for catheter or surgical intervention.

babies.medical_history: Born at 31+2 weeks; brief CPAP. Reached full formula feeds on day 12.
babies.condition_summary: Preterm boy, 18 days old, with necrotising enterocolitis and pneumatosis, worsening despite medical management.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 18. Weight 1560 g. Onset on 29 Oct with distension and bloody stool. X-ray: extensive pneumatosis intestinalis; repeat today shows a fixed dilated loop and possible portal venous gas, no definite free air. Platelets fell from 210 to 64 x10^9/L, CRP 96 mg/L, lactate 4.1 mmol/L. Back on CPAP, FiO2 0.30, for increased work of breathing. Nil by mouth on meropenem and metronidazole.

oxygen_support.notes: CPAP 6 cmH2O for increased work of breathing.

babies.current_care: Nil by mouth, nasogastric decompression, IV antibiotics, IV fluids.
babies.transfer_reason: Enterocolitis is deteriorating with signs of impending perforation and may need a laparotomy. The referring centre has no surgical or post-operative neonatal service.

babies.medical_history: Term girl; left congenital diaphragmatic hernia diagnosed on the 22-week scan (observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio 38%). Delivered at the referring centre after spontaneous labour.
babies.condition_summary: Term newborn, 2 hours old, with an antenatally diagnosed left diaphragmatic hernia, intubated at birth.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 0, 2 hours. Weight 2900 g. Intubated at birth without bag-mask ventilation; nasogastric tube on free drainage. Gentle ventilation: PIP 22, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.60. Pre-ductal SpO2 86%, post-ductal 78%. X-ray: bowel loops in the left hemithorax with mediastinal shift to the right. Mean BP 40 mmHg after a saline bolus.
babies.current_care: Ventilated, gastric decompression, sedation, IV fluids.
babies.transfer_reason: Antenatally diagnosed diaphragmatic hernia with significant pulmonary hypoplasia. Needs a surgical neonatal centre with advanced respiratory and pulmonary hypertension management.

babies.medical_history: Early-term boy; maternal polyhydramnios. Excess frothy secretions from birth.
babies.condition_summary: Term newborn, 1 day old, with oesophageal atresia and a distal tracheo-oesophageal fistula; feeding has not been started.
symptoms: tube coiled in the upper pouch on X-ray
babies.clinical_notes: Day 1. Weight 2560 g. 10 Fr Replogle tube coiled in the upper pouch at T3 on X-ray; gas in the stomach and bowel indicates a distal fistula. Continuous low-pressure suction. Breathing room air, SpO2 95%, mild tachypnoea 64/min. No other anomaly found on initial examination; echocardiography not yet done. IV fluids running.
babies.current_care: Head-up positioning, continuous upper-pouch suction, nil by mouth, IV fluids.
babies.transfer_reason: Needs surgical repair of the oesophageal atresia with fistula ligation, and cardiac screening before surgery. There is no neonatal surgical service at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Late preterm girl; gastroschisis found on the 20-week scan. Delivered vaginally at the referring centre.
babies.condition_summary: Late preterm newborn, 1 hour old, with gastroschisis; bowel covered and positioned to protect its blood supply.
symptoms: bowel exposed through an abdominal wall defect
babies.clinical_notes: Day 0, 1 hour. Weight 2300 g. Defect about 3 cm to the right of the umbilicus. Bowel pink and mildly thickened, no obvious atresia or necrosis. Placed in a sterile bowel bag, right lateral position, nasogastric tube on free drainage. Temperature 36.2 C. IV access obtained; 10 mL/kg saline bolus given. SpO2 97% in room air.
babies.current_care: Bowel bag, gastric decompression, IV fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics.
babies.transfer_reason: Gastroschisis needs closure or silo placement by a neonatal surgical team within hours, followed by prolonged intravenous nutrition.

babies.medical_history: Term boy, feeding well until day 3.
babies.condition_summary: Term boy, 3 days old, with sudden bilious vomiting; malrotation with volvulus cannot be excluded.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 3. Weight 3180 g. Three episodes of dark green vomiting since 06:00. Abdomen mildly distended and soft, no peritonism. Upright X-ray: paucity of distal bowel gas, no free air. Contrast study not available locally. Heart rate 168/min, capillary refill 3 seconds after a 10 mL/kg bolus. SpO2 98% in room air.
babies.current_care: Nil by mouth, nasogastric tube on free drainage, IV fluids.
babies.transfer_reason: Bilious vomiting in a newborn needs immediate contrast imaging and surgical assessment to exclude volvulus. Neither is available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Late preterm girl. Did not pass meconium until 52 hours, after rectal stimulation.
babies.condition_summary: Late preterm girl, 10 days old, with delayed meconium, recurrent abdominal distension and suspected Hirschsprung disease.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 10. Weight 2040 g. Recurrent distension relieved by rectal washouts. One episode of fever 38.4 C with foul-smelling diarrhoea on day 9, treated as enterocolitis with IV antibiotics; CRP 34 mg/L and now settling. Tolerating small feeds of 60 mL/kg/day. SpO2 98% in room air.
babies.current_care: Twice-daily rectal washouts, IV antibiotics, partial IV fluids.
babies.transfer_reason: Suspected Hirschsprung disease with one enterocolitis episode. Needs a rectal biopsy, contrast enema and surgical planning, which the referring centre cannot provide.

babies.medical_history: Term boy discharged on day 2. Re-admitted on day 8 with fever and lethargy.
babies.condition_summary: Term boy, 9 days old, with septic shock and suspected bacterial meningitis, needing two inotropes.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 9. Weight 2850 g. Lumbar puncture: CSF white cells 1250/uL (90% neutrophils), protein 2.4 g/L, glucose 0.9 mmol/L; Gram stain pending. Blood culture growing Gram-negative bacilli at 14 hours. On cefotaxime and amikacin. After 40 mL/kg of fluid, mean BP 32 mmHg; now on dopamine 10 and adrenaline 0.1 mcg/kg/min. Two seizures, loaded with phenobarbitone. Intubated for apnoea, FiO2 0.35.
babies.current_care: Ventilated, two inotropes, IV antibiotics, anticonvulsant.
babies.transfer_reason: Catecholamine-resistant shock with meningitis and seizures. Needs intensive multi-organ support, continuous brain monitoring and neurology input that are not available locally.

babies.medical_history: Born at 30+5 weeks; ventilated for 3 days, then CPAP for 7 days. Peripherally inserted central catheter for intravenous nutrition until day 21.
babies.condition_summary: Preterm girl, 26 days old, with a carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella bloodstream infection and falling platelets.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 26. Weight 1620 g. Blood culture (24 Oct): Klebsiella pneumoniae resistant to meropenem, sensitive only to colistin and tigecycline. Central line removed. Platelets 22 x10^9/L; one platelet transfusion given. CRP 142 mg/L. Back on CPAP 6 cmH2O, FiO2 0.30, for apnoeas. Two other infants share her room.
babies.current_care: CPAP, IV colistin, nil by mouth, platelet transfusion.
babies.transfer_reason: Multi-drug-resistant bloodstream infection that needs isolation nursing, specialist antimicrobial management and reliable blood product support. The referring unit cannot isolate her.

babies.medical_history: Late preterm boy; maternal fever of 38.6 C in labour and membranes ruptured for 26 hours. Mother was not screened for group B streptococcus.
babies.condition_summary: Late preterm boy, 2 days old, with early-onset sepsis and pneumonia, needing increasing respiratory support.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 2. Weight 2280 g. Blood culture: Gram-positive cocci in chains at 18 hours. On ampicillin and gentamicin since 2 hours of age. High-flow 8 L/min with FiO2 increasing to 0.50. X-ray: bilateral patchy opacities. Glucose 2.1 mmol/L twice; now on 10% dextrose at 80 mL/kg/day. Capillary refill 4 seconds; 20 mL/kg saline given.

oxygen_support.notes: High-flow nasal cannula 8 L/min, FiO2 increasing.

babies.current_care: High-flow support, IV antibiotics, IV dextrose, fluid boluses.
babies.transfer_reason: Respiratory failure with sepsis is getting worse. He will probably need intubation, ventilation and possibly inotropes, beyond what the referring centre can sustain.

babies.medical_history: Mother is Rh-negative and did not receive anti-D in her previous pregnancy. Baby is O Rh-positive with a strongly positive direct antiglobulin test.
babies.condition_summary: Term girl, 3 days old, with haemolytic disease from Rh isoimmunisation and bilirubin approaching the exchange threshold despite intensive phototherapy.
symptoms: deep jaundice extending to the soles
babies.clinical_notes: Day 3 (72 hours). Weight 2960 g. Total serum bilirubin 24.8 mg/dL, rising 0.6 mg/dL per hour over the last 6 hours, on double-surface phototherapy. Hb 10.2 g/dL, reticulocytes 12%. IV immunoglobulin 1 g/kg given 8 hours ago. No abnormal tone or high-pitched cry yet. Compatible blood is not available locally at short notice.
babies.current_care: Double-surface phototherapy, IV fluids, IV immunoglobulin.
babies.transfer_reason: Bilirubin is still rising despite intensive phototherapy and immunoglobulin. An exchange transfusion is likely within hours and cannot be performed at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Late preterm boy discharged on day 2, exclusively breastfed. Brought back on day 5 with yellow eyes and sleepiness. His father has G6PD deficiency.
babies.condition_summary: Late preterm boy, 5 days old, with severe jaundice, 10% weight loss and early abnormal tone; suspected G6PD-related haemolysis.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 5. Weight 2300 g (birth weight 2550 g). Total serum bilirubin 27.6 mg/dL. G6PD screen: deficient. Intermittent retrocollis and a high-pitched cry during examination, concerning for early acute bilirubin encephalopathy. Intensive phototherapy and IV fluids started. Hb 12.1 g/dL.
babies.current_care: Intensive phototherapy, IV fluids, feeding support.
babies.transfer_reason: Severe hyperbilirubinaemia with early neurological signs needs an immediate exchange transfusion and neurological follow-up, which are not available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Term girl, uneventful delivery, Apgar 9 and 10. An older sibling had seizures in infancy; cause never established.
babies.condition_summary: Term girl, 4 days old, with frequent seizures not controlled by two anticonvulsants and no history of birth asphyxia.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 4. Weight 3280 g. Seizures began on day 2: right-sided clonic jerks with eye deviation lasting 1-2 minutes, up to 8 per day. Phenobarbitone 40 mg/kg in total and levetiracetam 60 mg/kg given; still 4 seizures in the last 12 hours. Glucose, calcium, magnesium and sodium normal. CSF normal. Cranial ultrasound normal. Two seizure-related apnoeas needed brief bag-mask ventilation. Room air between events.
babies.current_care: Anticonvulsants, IV fluids, partial tube feeds.
babies.transfer_reason: Refractory seizures of unknown cause need continuous brain monitoring, an MRI and metabolic and genetic investigation, none of which are available at the referring centre.

babies.medical_history: Term boy, born to parents who are second-degree relatives; well for the first 3 days. An older sibling died at 10 days of age with an undiagnosed illness.
babies.condition_summary: Term boy, 6 days old, with encephalopathy and very high ammonia; suspected inborn error of metabolism.
babies.clinical_notes: Day 6. Weight 2950 g. Ammonia 612 umol/L, 690 umol/L on repeat at 4 hours. Blood gas pH 7.52, pCO2 26 mmHg. Glucose 4.6 mmol/L, no ketones. Feeds stopped; 10% dextrose at 150 mL/kg/day started. Ammonia-scavenging medication not available locally. Becoming less responsive; intubation may soon be needed.
babies.current_care: Nil by mouth, high-glucose IV infusion, close neurological observation.
babies.transfer_reason: Severe hyperammonaemia needs immediate ammonia-removal therapy, possibly dialysis, and metabolic specialist care. None of these are available at the referring centre.
